content: This review is part of a series that evaluates various methods for cervical ripening and induction of labor using standardized methodologies. The objective of this specific review was to assess the effects of oral prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) for inducing labor in the third trimester of pregnancy. The search for relevant studies was conducted using the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group's Trials Register up to January 2007, and additional references were identified from bibliographies of related papers. An updated search was performed on June 8, 2012, and the results were added to a section awaiting classification for further analysis. The review included clinical trials that compared oral PGE2 for third-trimester cervical ripening or labor induction with placebo, no treatment, or other predefined methods of labor induction. A two-stage data extraction strategy was employed to manage the large volume and complexity of trial data. A total of 19 studies were included in the review. Of these, 15 studies involved comparisons using either oral or intravenous oxytocin, with or without amniotomy. The overall quality of the studies was low. Only seven studies clearly described allocation concealment, and only two studies reported blinding of providers, participants, or both to the treatment groups. For the outcome of vaginal delivery not achieved within 24 hours, a composite comparison of oral PGE2 versus all oxytocin treatments (oral and intravenous, with and without amniotomy) showed a trend favoring oxytocin treatments, though the result was not statistically significant (relative risk [RR] 1.97, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.86 to 4.48). For the outcome of cesarean section, oral PGE2 was favored over no treatment or placebo (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.98). However, for other outcomes, there were no significant differences between the groups. Oral PGE2 was consistently associated with gastrointestinal side effects, particularly vomiting, across all comparison groups. The authors concluded that oral prostaglandin E2 did not demonstrate clear advantages over other methods of labor induction and was associated with more frequent gastrointestinal adverse effects. It is noted that six citations in the awaiting classification section of the review may influence the conclusions once they are assessed.
